candidates.label: Subscription model: once-free workouts now locked; value is split
candidates.description: Long-time users say the core daily workouts moved behind a paywall or free-access limit, calling it a 'money grab'; others still report the app works without paying or has been worth paying for. This conflict is the strongest signal in the data.
candidates.quote: now everything is behind a paywall

candidates.label: AI-generated content and stale workouts feel like quality decline
candidates.description: Several reviewers describe AI slop, AI mockups, unrealistic AI women, and recycled workouts replacing the old experience; one suspects honest critical reviews are removed, deepening distrust.
candidates.quote: ai slop everywhere

candidates.label: User requests: more free access, longer intervals, true personalization
candidates.description: Reviewers explicitly ask for more free courses or ad-based access, longer interval times, routines that genuinely respect limitations such as knee avoidance, honest 'free' labeling, and an easier way to cancel renewals.
candidates.quote: i just wish there were more free courses, or the option to watch an add to use all of the courses that are premium.

candidates.label: Billing, renewals, and ad screens create trust-breaking friction
candidates.description: Separate from the general paywall complaint, users report concrete monetization friction: trial charged without clear reminder, yearly renewal impossible to cancel via the app/support, and an ad screen that can't be exited.
candidates.quote: there’s no way to get out of it and proceed to the app

candidates.label: Workout format loved, but plan personalization and inconsistency frustrate
candidates.description: The short 30–45 second format, at-home flexibility, and variety are repeatedly praised; conversely, users report that plan personalization fails (knees still get squats/lunges), the daily routine can repeat legs without arms, settings reset, and one user felt no ab engagement.
candidates.quote: i love that each exercise is only 30-45 seconds

candidates.label: Free workouts moved behind paywall
candidates.description: A large cluster of reviews report that workouts that used to be free — including previously saved workouts — now require a paid subscription, leaving users unable to exercise without paying.
candidates.quote: even workouts i had previously saved now ask you to pay

candidates.label: Positive outcomes: motivating, effective, and life-changing for loyal users
candidates.description: Loyal users report real results—weight loss, soreness, motivation, convenience—and some call it a literal life saver; this positive value is important context for the subscription debate.
candidates.quote: it’s been a literal life saver

candidates.label: Subscription value is polarizing
candidates.description: The paid model splits long-time users: some call the subscription fair and worth the money, while others describe it as an unreasonable pay-to-feel-proud experience and refuse to pay for what used to be free.
candidates.quote: i’ve had this app for over five years now and i’ve loved them, but hate how they kept going from completely free to charging for everything now. really great app but not paying for it

candidates.label: Misleading trial billing and unexpected charges
candidates.description: Several users describe being charged sooner than expected, not being warned before a trial ended, and having trouble finding or canceling subscription details after payment.
candidates.quote: i subscribed to what i thought was a year plan for 39.99 and a 6 day trial. it did not let me know before the trail was over so i couldn’t cancel it

candidates.label: Paid users locked out and support unreachable
candidates.description: Paying subscribers report being logged out, unable to log back in, unable to access purchased benefits, and unable to get help because support messages are blocked as spam or email sending fails.
candidates.quote: i paid for a year membership and i cannot log into the account because it says it does not exist

candidates.label: Workout variety and motivation earn praise
candidates.description: Many positive reviews highlight the range of workout types and levels, easy-to-follow routines, warm-ups, cool-downs, and motivational structure that help users stay consistent at home.
candidates.quote: it has everything from face yoga to military style workouts

candidates.label: Ads and Shein redirects interrupt workouts
candidates.description: Some users report forced ads during workouts and, in the most severe cases, the app closing mid-exercise and opening the Shein website repeatedly without user interaction, making workouts unusable.
candidates.quote: the app will close and the shein website will open

candidates.label: Free-trial billing and cancellation traps
candidates.description: Users report being charged immediately for a supposedly free trial, receiving charges after canceling, and struggling to manage or cancel subscriptions. This is the strongest source of anger and trust loss.
candidates.quote: cancelled my subscription and then received not one but two charges in the same day totaling almost $100!!!

candidates.label: Paywalled free tier and premium-upgrade friction
candidates.description: Several users hit a hard paywall after day one, lose previously free routines, or face full-screen premium prompts. Even users who like the workouts dislike being blocked from basic use.
candidates.quote: now everything i click on they want you to subscribe and that sucks

candidates.label: Workout quality, variety, and clear programming
candidates.description: Many reviewers praise the app for thoughtfully sequenced exercises, a wide variety of routines, and options for different goals such as dumbbells, yoga, pilates, and postpartum recovery. This is the core reason users stay.
candidates.quote: genuinely well thought out, really nicely put together

candidates.label: Short, beginner-friendly workouts for busy schedules
candidates.description: Users value sessions that are 20 minutes or less and sustainable for beginners, making it easier to stay consistent around work and family.
candidates.quote: i can fit 20 min or less anytime in between my schedule

candidates.label: Subscription value is polarizing
candidates.description: The same membership is seen as a cheap gym replacement by devoted users, while others call it a waste or resent paying for what used to be free. This is the clearest love/hate split in the data.
candidates.quote: i think it’s great but i hate that we have to pay just to work out

candidates.label: Content requests and unmet needs
candidates.description: Power users want new programs, more exercise options, and content for younger users. These are direct expansion opportunities.
candidates.quote: i do wish they’d put out some new programs, though i’m sure at some point they will

candidates.label: Subscription value is polarizing: results vs paywall lockout
candidates.description: Free and long-time users report that formerly accessible workouts are now locked behind a subscription and call the pricing 'ridiculous', while a subscriber credits the paid plan with completely transforming their body composition. The same monetization model is seen as either worth it or as a bait-and-switch.
candidates.quote: i have consistently done my program 2x per week since and i have completely transformed my body composition.

candidates.label: Misleading free trial and surprise charges
candidates.description: Users report being charged on the same day they sign up despite an advertised free trial, and then not receiving responses or refunds. This creates a trust problem around the subscription offer.
candidates.quote: i was charged the same day i signed up and wasn’t given the advertised 3 days free.

candidates.label: Intrusive ads and broken free-with-ads tier
candidates.description: The ad experience is causing workout interruptions, including a redirect to an outside shopping site, and the advertised free-with-ads option is not actually offered, leaving users stuck between intrusive ads and a paid plan.
candidates.quote: i was redirected to the shein website three times during a recent workout.

candidates.label: Workout content variety: loved by some, repetitive for others
candidates.description: Some users praise the freshness, variations, and added movements in the workouts, while others feel newer daily workouts are repetitive and that routines like 'daily habit stretch' are mislabeled. This usability/content tension is a polarizing part of the workout experience.
candidates.quote: many of the newer daily workouts are the same things over and over.

candidates.label: Workout guidance is strong, but customization and tracking controls are missing
candidates.description: Users like the easy-to-follow, distraction-free guided setup, but ask for more control: connect to Apple Watch for automatic calorie counting, switch from timers to rep counting, and offer less wordy audio cues for users who bring their own music.
candidates.quote: i wished i could connect it to my watch so that i counts the calories i burned instead of just doing it manually.

candidates.label: Missing pregnancy-safe workout category
candidates.description: A highly engaged user notes there are stretch and postpartum options but almost nothing safe for pregnancy or by trimester, which feels like a gap for a women's fitness app. This is a concrete expansion opportunity.
candidates.quote: there is a lack of pregnancy safe strength training, mobility and flexibility workouts.

candidates.label: Free-trial signup results in immediate unexpected charges
candidates.description: Several users were charged immediately when signing up for a 'free trial' or 'pay nothing now' plan, including yearly charges, and couldn't find support or a refund. This creates a strong trust problem and feels misleading.
candidates.quote: i got charged $52.99 instantly for the year when that option was not even highlighted

candidates.label: Aggressive, hard-to-dismiss ads ruin the free workout experience
candidates.description: Free-tier users describe 90-second ads, unclear close buttons, and ads that force them to force-quit the app. The ad experience is seen as punishment and pushes users to uninstall.
candidates.quote: they’ve hidden the x button so that when the 90s ad finishes, you can’t even get out of the ad without force closing the whole app

candidates.label: Personalization is valued, but mandatory weight-loss goals exclude other fitness motivations
candidates.description: Workout customization based on age, weight, and struggles is a major strength, yet the app forces a weight-loss goal and attaches weight-loss notes to exercises. Users who want flexibility or general health find this alienating and potentially harmful, especially for teens.
candidates.quote: every single exercise comes with a note on how much weight you’ll lose.

candidates.label: Workout length and difficulty: convenient and gentle for some, too easy for others
candidates.description: Short guided workouts are praised as easy to fit into busy schedules and accessible for beginners or older users, but at least one user finds even the hardest setting too easy and wants more challenge.
candidates.quote: even if it’s up to all the way, it’s not that hard

candidates.label: Workout guidance and music options are standout positives, with room for more music variety
candidates.description: Users value the on-screen demonstrator, motivating music, ability to connect third-party music apps, and song skipping. The main request is greater music variety within the app.
candidates.quote: the music that is provided is nice so i don’t have to overlap another app to play music (and you can skip songs) wish there was more of a variety of songs though

candidates.label: Forced 90-second ads enrage free users but some accept them for results
candidates.description: The most repeated complaint is that the free tier now forces a 90+ second ad before every workout, with users calling it excessive, scammy, and demotivating. One 5-star reviewer still loves the app and credits it for losing 25 pounds in 3 months, showing the same ad gate is polarizing rather than universally unacceptable.
candidates.quote: now you have to watch a 90 second ad before every workout unless you’d rather pay for premium

candidates.label: Subscription value polarizes: worth every penny vs bait-and-switch paywall
candidates.description: Some paying users say the app is worth the money and cheaper than a gym membership, while many others feel misled by the 'free' label after onboarding funnels them into a 7-day trial or a $40/year subscription. The conflict is strongest around affordability and perceived honesty of the free tier.
candidates.quote: says it’s free, but it makes you go through a ton of steps, then gives you no way to continue without paying $40/yr.

candidates.label: Workout quality is polarizing: life-changing effectiveness vs AI slop and low intensity
candidates.description: Many users praise the workouts for producing real results, building habits, and offering effective short routines. In sharp contrast, a long-time paying member says most workouts are now 'AI slop' with mismatched voice and diagram cues, while another intermediate user doesn't feel enough burn. This is a core polarizing tension around workout usability and content quality.
candidates.quote: most of the workouts are just ai slop now

candidates.label: Data sync, cross-device access, and support failures
candidates.description: Users report losing tracked progress after switching phones, no login option on Android tablet despite a paid subscription, Apple Watch Series 11 not registering workouts as exercise, and emails going unanswered. These reliability and support gaps undermine trust in paid users and represent a clear opportunity to improve account continuity.
candidates.quote: just got a new phone and none of the data loaded to my new device, even with my log in

candidates.label: Unmet requests: more abs work, YouTube Music, and clearer exercise demos
candidates.description: Explicit opportunity signals include requests for more abdominal exercises, support for YouTube Music playlists (Spotify linking is already celebrated), and better visual instruction for how to perform moves. Filling these gaps could increase premium willingness and reduce beginners' friction.
candidates.quote: i wish that you guys had youtube music on there that we could choose from

candidates.label: Subscription value and billing: paywall backlash vs. worth-it praise
candidates.description: The subscription model is the most polarizing aspect. A large cluster of users are angry that free access has been removed, report unexpected charges after 'free trials' or cancelled memberships, and describe a confusing set of subscription options. Others explicitly say the app is worth it and the paid/free content keeps them on track.
candidates.quote: it would not let you access the free workouts unless you signed up for a “free trial.” it said i would not be charged at the time of subscribing but it charged my card $39.99 for a yearly subscription

candidates.label: Exercise avoidance and personalization not honored
candidates.description: Users who specify areas to avoid (e.g., abs) still receive workouts targeting those areas, and the onboarding quiz appears not to influence the generated plan. This leads to frustration and distrust in the app's personalization.
candidates.quote: asks what to avoid but still includes moves that aggravate that area.

warnings.message: kept 36 of 81 discovered candidates (goal-aware selection); 45 excess dropped deterministically
